proposedOperatorData.name: Antur Stiniog
proposedOperatorData.tagline: Community-run downhill MTB uplift centre with 14 gravity trails in the Blaenau Ffestiniog slate hills
proposedOperatorData.description:
Antur Stiniog is a not-for-profit social enterprise, founded in 2007, running a downhill mountain bike uplift centre on the slopes above the former Llechwedd Slate Caverns in Blaenau Ffestiniog, Eryri (Snowdonia). It offers a van-based uplift service (widely regarded as one of the best in the UK) giving riders access to 14 gravity-fed trails cut through slate quarry terrain, ranging from beginner-friendly blues to advanced reds and blacks, with up to 20 runs possible in a day.

On-site facilities include bike hire (Saracen downhill bikes), a bike shop, bike wash and showers, a kids' club, and the Ty Coffi Antur 'Stiniog cafe (independently rated 4.8/5 on TripAdvisor). As a social enterprise, profits are reinvested in the local community and in environmental partnerships, including woodland restoration work with Y Dref Werdd.

The centre is a fixture of the UK downhill MTB scene, drawing repeat visitors for its distinctive rock-and-shale trail character and fast, reliable uplift turnaround.
proposedOperatorData.uniqueSellingPoint: Community-owned social enterprise MTB uplift centre widely cited as running the best downhill uplift service in the UK, set on former slate quarry terrain unique to North Wales.
